chunks: And from him, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Maintain your kinship ties, even if it be with the greeting (as-salam).'
Allah, Blessed and High is He, says: 'And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the kinship; surely Allah was Ever-Watchful over you.'
ai.seo_question: How can one maintain family ties if communication is difficult?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes that maintaining kinship (silat al-rahim) is obligatory even if it requires only the minimal act of offering a greeting (taslim), ensuring no complete severance occurs. This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility in fulfilling this duty, linking the social obligation directly to divine accountability as noted in the Quranic verse 4:1. In Shia tradition, this underscores that even strained relationships must be preserved through basic courtesy to avoid the spiritual penalty of cutting ties.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Maintain your kinship even though it be with the greetings.
Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying [4:1] and fear Allah, by Whom you are asking by Him and the kinship; surely Allah was Ever-Watchful over you’.
en.sarwar: 22. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from al-Qasim ibn Y ahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘One must maintain good relations with relatives. Even offering the greeting of peace should not be held back from them.

Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, says, “Have fear of the One by whose name you swear to settle your differences and have respect for your relatives. Allah certainly keeps watch over you.’” [4:1]
